The abdominal x-ray demonstrates the classic "double bubble" appearance consistent with proximal duodenal obstruction. The dysmorphic features (epicanthus, upslanting palpebral fissures, single transverse palmar crease, low-set ears) and a congenital heart murmur strongly suggest Down syndrome (trisomy 21), which is commonly associated with duodenal atresia (failed duodenal recanalization; annular pancreas is another related cause). DIAGNOSIS: Duodenal atresia (likely associated with Down syndrome)
